topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: I move through the underbrush, my heart pounding louder than the thud of my paws. The air is heavy with the scent of rain and the rustle of leaves is a cacophony of warnings. There is an old, familiar smell on the wind — something soft and worn, carrying a hint of the past. But there is no time to linger, no comfort to be found. My sides heave with each labored breath, the forest seems to close in, tighter and tighter. I must keep moving, must find shelter, must escape the shadows that stretch and snarl with the fading light. The ground beneath my feet is uneven, treacherous. Every step is a gamble, but I cannot stop. The old, faint scent fades, lost to the urgency of now.
